fields.status: Official history observed November 5, 2026 lists the House passed the bill on 2026-03-18; the Senate Energy Committee reported and recommitted it on 2026-06-10. Later disposition and current legal force were not independently established by this review.
fields.key_provisions: Senate-recommitted substitute proposes data-center electric-service tariffs and cost allocation, water measurement and reporting, public-records and nondisclosure rules, wastewater monitoring and tax-incentive conditions. Chapter 4941 covers primarily or exclusively digital-information uses, including virtual-currency mining, on single or contiguous/adjacent/aggregated parcels, with peak demand greater than 25 MW at a single building or physical location; specified supply requirements concern new centers with aggregate monthly maximum demand greater than 250 MW. Sections 4941.02-.04 have exceptions for qualifying pre-effective-date utility contracts, subject to a commission-determined material-capacity-increase rule, and specified treatment for contracts under previously approved data-center tariffs.

fields.key_provisions: Introduced proposal establishes data-center customer requirements including minimum 12-year contracts, exit payments, unused-capacity charges and financial assurances. It restricts recovering related costs from other customer classes unless PUCO finds the recovery just and reasonable; specified contract and cost-recovery approvals separately require a finding that rates for other existing customers will not increase.

fields.key_provisions: Introduced proposal restricts public incentives and siting for defined new data centers and assigns developer electric-cost responsibilities. Public land and platted residential neighborhoods are restricted; prime farmland has an exception requiring both voluntary sale and a county-commission resolution authorizing construction. Approval, permitting and interconnection provisions include specified rate-impact showings, presumptions and exceptions.
